title_or_table: 2024 Annual Survey of School System Finances: Public Elementary-Secondary Education Finances, Fiscal Year 2024, summary tables and all data items file
table_id: elsec24_sumtables.xlsx Tables 1, 5, 8, 11 and 19; elsec24.txt items AR1, AR1A, AR1B, AR2, AR2A, AR3, AR6, AR6A and TFEDREV
observation_period: Fiscal year 2024 (school year 2023 to 2024); enrollment, fall 2023
universe_or_base: Public school systems, independent and dependent, as the Bureau defines them; charter schools whose charters a nongovernmental entity holds are out of scope
unit: per the unit column: thousands of dollars, percent, dollars or students
vintage: Fiscal year 2024 summary tables and data files
qualification: Federal revenue includes COVID-19 relief funds, which the Bureau’s documentation says are included; summed from its all data items file they come to $39.2 billion of the $115.1 billion federal revenue. Per-pupil figures exclude adult education, community services and other programs outside elementary-secondary schooling. Table 13’s row reads Fall enrollment, 2022 and its note fall 2022, but prints Table 19’s fall 2023 figure; this file takes Table 19.

code.description: USPS state code, US for the nation

value.description: the figure; percents and per-pupil dollars stored to four decimals

printed_source_line: Source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2024 Annual Survey of School System Finances, fiscal 2024, public school systems, United States. Retrieved November 12, 2026. Federal revenue includes $39.2 billion in COVID-19 relief funds.
